## 17. CARD MODE ADDENDUM

output_mode is card_mode: the text fills a short card for a Manager / Strategic Decision Maker
(for example in local government or insurance), shown with four stat tiles and two dashboard
panels (01: map of the 20 most geographically sensitive LSOAs with the expert-highlighted
regions; 02: what the model relies on by feature category, Hull-wide against the contrast area
in manager_overview.contrast_area). This section replaces section 14 "Length and form" and its
bolding rule. Every other section, including prohibited claims, the evidence-review "next step"
rule and the self-check, still applies.

The card combines both branches: the Feature branch says WHAT the model relies on, the Geo
branch says WHERE it is most sensitive to an area's location. Keep the two apart in wording.

Plain language for this reader: do not cite Moran's I, p-values, LISA class names, coefficients,
correlation values or other test statistics. GeoSensitivity values, ranks, shares, counts and
"N times" ratios are fine. Never write that the model "relies on" or "depends on" an area; it is
sensitive to an area's location. Name areas by locality; no street names.

Return ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:

- "headline": one sentence, at most 20 words: the single most decision-relevant finding that
  answers user_question.
- "tiles": exactly 4 objects {"value": ..., "label": ...}. value is one figure from the
  evidence (at most 8 characters, e.g. "61%", "18/20"); label is at most 10 plain words that
  make the figure meaningful on its own to a reader who has not read the text: say what it
  measures in everyday words ("of the model's reasoning", not "share of local importance") and,
  where the evidence allows, what it is compared with (e.g. "against 20% Hull-wide"). A count
  is written as a fraction of its whole ("10/30", not "10"). One tile each for: what drives
  the model, the exception, what can be set aside, and confidence.
- "section_01": at most 70 words, drivers and exceptions (panel 02): what the model relies on
  across Hull (manager_overview.drivers), then the contrast area by locality name: what leads it
  and how it differs from Hull, and where such areas sit in GeoSensitivity
  (drivers.not_crime_led). Mention Old Town only as the GeoSensitivity exception, in one clause.
  The tiles carry the counts; do not restate how many areas the six-month average leads.
- "section_02": at most 60 words, what can be set aside and how far to trust it: name three of
  the set-aside candidates in plain words (manager_overview.set_aside.features) and their
  combined share, without restating how many there are (the tile gives it); add the caveat in
  plain words; then end with one
  clause saying the most sensitive areas agree with the expert's regions, pointing to panel 01
  for the count. No chance comparison, no stability or across-model remarks and no next-step
  sentence: this replaces the section 9 next-step item for this card.
- "footer": one limitation, at most 15 words, ruling out causal or resourcing readings.

No repetition: every figure appears ONCE on the card. The panels already print the figures
in manager_overview.shown_on_panels (the expert agreement in panel 01's title and the category
shares in panel 02), so neither tiles nor sections may cite them; refer to the panel in words
instead ("as panel 02 shows"). A tile figure is not cited again in the sections, not even its first number
("144/168" on a tile rules out "144 areas" in the text).

Key-term counts: 1-2 in the headline and 2-4 in EACH section. Tiles and footer carry no
markup.

Highlighting markup (you choose what to mark):

- wrap every figure you cite as [[n:...]], e.g. [[n:14%]];
- wrap the key terms a planner should catch when scanning as [[t:...]]. This is required,
  not optional: keep to the counts given above, each at most 4 words (the finding phrase
  itself, the leading feature names, or the key place names). Before answering, count the
  [[t:...]] spans and fix any count outside the range;
- no other markup and no markdown bold.

Every figure must be copied or rounded from EVIDENCE_JSON (shares as percentages:
0.139 -> 14%). Do not compute new figures and do not cite a figure that is not supplied.

ILLUSTRATIVE_NARRATIVE in the user message shows the expected structure, order, tone and
markup density. It is an example of wording, not evidence: take every figure from
EVIDENCE_JSON, and write your own sentences.

illustrative_narrative.section_01: As panel 02 shows, the model reads Hull mainly through [[t:crime history]], then census characteristics. [[t:East Ella]] is the reverse: other features lead. It is one of [[n:22]] areas not led by crime history, and these are [[t:rarely where the model is most sensitive]]: the highest of them ranks [[n:30]]. Old Town remains the sensitivity exception.
illustrative_narrative.section_02: Road density, intersection density and nightlife count are among the [[t:candidates to set aside]]: each carries under [[n:1%]], all of them together [[n:7%]] of local importance. Related count and density measures can share weight, so judge them as groups. The areas where the model is most sensitive agree with [[t:local expertise]] (panel 01).
illustrative_narrative.footer: Describes what the model uses, not causes of crime or where to put resources.

global_geo.note: GeoSensitivity is the Geo-branch random-donor SMILE coefficient: masking an LSOA moves its rows to the centroids of random other Hull LSOAs (50 draws, all other inputs kept), and the coefficient attributes the resulting prediction shift to that LSOA. Absolute shifts are larger where predicted crime is higher. It is not latitude or longitude feature attribution.

global_spatial_pattern.note: LISA classes describe clustering of signed GeoSensitivity (random-donor design). They are not crime hotspots and not latitude/longitude effects.
global_spatial_pattern.lisa_counts_unit: number of LSOAs in each LISA class, not number of clusters

evaluation.att_stability_note: Controlled-input ATT stability. Distinct from multi-run Consistency.

consistency.definition: Multi-run explanation consistency across seeds (consistency_seed_base=100). Pairwise Rank Spearman, Score Pearson, and Top-20% Jaccard of |coefficients|. Not controlled-input ATT stability.

geo_design.name: random_donor
geo_design.definition: Random-donor design: masking an LSOA moves the coordinates of its rows to the centroid of a random other Hull LSOA (K = 50 draws), all other inputs kept; response is Wasserstein-1 on the affected LSOA-month predictions of the XGBoost model on 30 predictors + easting/northing; LSOAs ranked by the signed Geo-SMILE coefficient.

sign_conventions.local_feature_coefficient: Directional. Masks code a retained player as one and the response is the perturbed minus the original prediction, so a positive value means the area's own value of the feature raises its prediction relative to the masking reference and a negative value lowers it.
sign_conventions.global_feature_coefficient: Not directional: fitted to a non-negative distance; rank by magnitude.
sign_conventions.geo_coefficient: Relative contribution to the coalition response; the sign is not a direction of crime.
sign_conventions.feature_branch_model: One XGBoost model on the substantive predictors plus the centroid coordinates; coordinates are kept at their true values and are not Feature players.

limitations: No RAG / no invented local context.

set_aside.caveat: low weight in this model, not irrelevance in reality; count and density versions of the same measure can split weight, so judge them as groups (related_group_share)

seeds.plain_reading: the area ranking is very stable across runs; the order of features below the top few is less stable (evaluation.consistency)

across_models.plain_reading: more accurate models gave closer agreement with expert judgement

limitations: Attribution describes what the model uses, not causes of crime or a basis for resourcing.
Census characteristics (for example unemployment, long-term sickness) can act as proxies for protected groups; any use beyond explanation needs a fairness review.

content.section_01: Panel 02 shows [[t:crime history]] is the main driver across Hull, with census and built environment features next. [[t:East Ella]] stands out: seasonality and unemployment lead there, not crime history. Only [[n:22]] areas are not crime-led, and these rarely coincide with the most geographically sensitive places—the highest ranks [[n:30]]. [[t:Old Town]] is the clear outlier for geographic sensitivity.
content.section_02: [[t:Road density]], intersection density, and nightlife count are among the [[t:set-aside candidates]], each under [[n:1%]] of local importance and together [[n:8%]]. Related count and density features can split weight, so consider them as groups. The most sensitive areas match [[t:expert-identified regions]] (see panel 01).
content.footer: This shows what the model uses, not causes of crime or resourcing advice.
